title: Explicit startup initialization
use_when: A startup POU initializes application state through explicitly configured warm/cold system tasks.
assumptions: G_Ready and G_State already exist as compatible resource globals.
Assign this POU to the intended startup task; retention policy is project-specific.
Do not reset retained production counters or calibration values without a requirement.
checks: Set Ready only after the application has actually established its initialization conditions.

title: Request edge with startup suppression
use_when: Generate one request pulse per deliberate false-to-true transition; suppress an already-high request on the first scan.
assumptions: These variables are non-retained locals unless the application explicitly requires otherwise.
A request pulse is not a stop command.
checks: Connect xRequest to the intended application request.
Call every scan of the owning cyclic task.
Reset/rearm behavior must match the consuming function block.

title: Nonblocking two-stage handshake
use_when: Coordinate two application operations using completion and error inputs without waiting in a WHILE loop.
assumptions: AckA/AckB describe the current operation, not stale completion bits.
Requests and acknowledgments are mapped to real project code separately.
Add a project-approved timeout for each wait state.
checks: Every wait returns control to the cyclic task.
Define timeout, abort and retry requirements.
Application request outputs are not physical safety outputs.

title: Cyclic Enable/Valid position reader
use_when: Read an existing logical axis position and latch errors without issuing motion commands.
assumptions: Axis is an existing correctly configured global AXIS_REF.
MC_ReadActualPosition matches the installed firmware interface.
MonitorEnable is controlled by application readiness.
checks: Call cyclically; do not equate a retained last position with current validity.
Check logical AxisNum and user units before consuming position.
